{"metadata":{"description":"DeepSeek Harness plugin: an MCP status button in the chat header showing which MCP servers answer right now","id":"gh:1438279069","install_available":true,"language":"Python","name":"dsh-mcp-status","slug":"lobichshev-ops/dsh-mcp-status","topics":["1c","deepseek-harness","dsh","dsh-plugin","mcp","model-context-protocol"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"DeepSeek Harness plugin: an MCP status button in the chat header showing which MCP servers answer ri"},{"id":"p1s2","text":"k Harness plugin: an MCP status button in the chat header showing which MCP servers answer right now"},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-mcp-status"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"**English** · Русский"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"> A DeepSeek Harness plugin that puts an **MCP** button in the chat header.
> One click and you see "},{"id":"p4s2","text":"which MCP servers are connected — and which of them
> answer *right now*, with the number of tools e"},{"id":"p4s3","text":"ach one actually exposes."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"*Example servers, addresses and names in the screenshot are placeholders.*"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"## Contents"},{"id":"p7s1","text":"- Why this exists
- What you get
- How it works
- Wire format
- States
- Configuration
- Installatio"},{"id":"p7s2","text":"n
- Standalone probe
- Troubleshooting
- Limitations
- License"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"## Why this exists"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"DSH connects MCP servers once, at startup. When one of them is down, the
symptoms are indirect: a to"},{"id":"p9s2","text":"ol that used to be in the model's toolset is simply
not there, or a call fails with a transport erro"},{"id":"p9s3","text":"r. The configuration file only
tells you what *should* be connected, not what is."},{"id":"p10s1","text":"An endpoint that holds a TCP port but never completes the MCP handshake looks
"up" to any port check"},{"id":"p10s2","text":"er. This plugin answers a stricter question: **does the
server complete `initialize` + `tools/list` "},{"id":"p10s3","text":"right now, and how many tools does
it return?** That is the same thing the Harness itself needs in o"},{"id":"p10s4","text":"rder to give
the model those tools."},{"id":"p11s1","text":"## What you get"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"| Element | Where | What it shows |"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"| Status pill | chat header, `conversation.session.header.utilities` | a dot: green when everything "},{"id":"p13s2","text":"answers, red when something is dead |
| Server list | inside the popover | name, endpoint, state, re"},{"id":"p13s3","text":"sponse time, tool count |
| EDT block | inside the popover | which `1C:EDT` projects are currently s"},{"id":"p13s4","text":"erving MCP, discovered from each project's `.mcp.json` |
| Refresh button | popover header | forces "},{"id":"p13s5","text":"a probe; the timestamp changes when the new result lands |"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"The answer is cached, so opening the panel is instant even though a full probe
takes ~15 seconds."},{"id":"p15s1","text":"## How it works"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"Two halves in one package — the usual shape for a DSH plugin with a UI."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"### Host half — `index.js`"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"Declares `export const inject = ['webServer']`, registers the route inside
`ctx.effect`, and runs th"},{"id":"p19s2","text":"e probe at startup and then every five minutes. The
probe is a child process: it writes JSON to a fi"},{"id":"p19s3","text":"le, the plugin reads that file,
caches it and serves it."},{"id":"p20s1","text":"### Client half — `client.js`"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"A classic script that registers itself through `window.__ModuleLoader__.load`
and exports `{ inject:"},{"id":"p21s2","text":" ['slots'], apply(ctx) }`. It places a React component
into the `conversation.session.header.utiliti"},{"id":"p21s3","text":"es` slot — the same band as the
locale and Markdown controls. The component polls the route on mount"},{"id":"p21s4","text":", then
every 20 seconds; while the host reports `refreshing: true` it polls every
1.5 seconds, so th"},{"id":"p21s5","text":"e timestamp changes the moment the result is ready instead of
half a minute later."},{"id":"p22s1","text":"### A handshake and not a port check"},{"id":"p23s1","text":"For every configured server the probe performs a real MCP handshake:"},{"id":"p24s1","text":"1. `POST initialize` with `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`, following
the `307` redirec"},{"id":"p24s2","text":"t some servers answer on `/mcp` before `/mcp/`.
2. Capture `Mcp-Session-Id` and send `notifications/"},{"id":"p24s3","text":"initialized` — several
FastMCP-based servers reject `tools/list` with *"Invalid request parameters"*"},{"id":"p24s4","text":"
without it.
3. `POST tools/list` with that session header; parse either a plain JSON body or
an SSE"},{"id":"p24s5","text":" stream (`data: {...}` blocks).
4. For `stdio` servers: spawn the configured command, speak newline-"},{"id":"p24s6","text":"delimited
JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout, with separate timeouts per stage — a router can
take 12 second"},{"id":"p24s7","text":"s on `tools/list` because it rescans its port range first."},{"id":"p25s1","text":"### Why a Python child process"},{"id":"p26s1","text":"That logic already exists as a tested Python script (`scripts/mcp_status.py`,
standard library only)"},{"id":"p26s2","text":". Re-implementing the transport edge cases in JavaScript
would create a second source of truth, so t"},{"id":"p26s3","text":"he host half simply runs the script
and caches its JSON. The script ships inside the package — no ex"},{"id":"p26s4","text":"y runs the script
and caches its JSON. The script ships inside the package — no external
dependency."},{"id":"p27s1","text":"One consequence worth knowing: the child's stdout is **not** captured through a
pipe. The script wri"},{"id":"p27s2","text":"tes its result to a file (`--out`), the plugin reads and
deletes it. Pipes are fragile under sandbox"},{"id":"p27s3","text":"ed shells; a file handoff works
everywhere."},{"id":"p28s1","text":"## Wire format"},{"id":"p29s1","text":"`GET /plugin/mcp-status` returns the cache envelope:"},{"id":"p30s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p31s1","text":"*Addresses above are examples and do not belong to any real network.*"},{"id":"p32s1","text":"`?refresh=1` starts a background probe and immediately returns the previous
cache with `refreshing: "},{"id":"p32s2","text":"true`. The UI keeps polling until `refreshing` flips
back."},{"id":"p33s1","text":"## States"},{"id":"p34s1","text":"| State | Meaning |"},{"id":"p35s1","text":"| `ok` | Handshake succeeded; `tools` is what the server returned. |
| `warn` | `initialize` succeed"},{"id":"p35s2","text":"ed, `tools/list` failed: alive but broken. `detail` carries the reason. |
| `dead` | Connection refu"},{"id":"p35s3","text":"sed, timeout, HTTP error, or a non-MCP response. |
| `off` | The config row has `disabled: true`. |
"},{"id":"p35s4","text":"| `skipped` | Not probed (for example an EDT project without a URL). |"},{"id":"p36s1","text":"## Configuration"},{"id":"p37s1","text":"All keys are optional and live in the loader row:"},{"id":"p38s1","text":"| Key | Default | Meaning |"},{"id":"p39s1","text":"| `pythonPath` | the DSH runtime Python | Interpreter for the probe script. |
| `scriptPath` | `scri"},{"id":"p39s2","text":"pts/mcp_status.py` in the package | Your own copy if you change the probe. |
| `intervalMs` | `30000"},{"id":"p39s3","text":"0` (5 min) | Background refresh period; minimum 15 s. |"},{"id":"p40s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p41s1","text":"## Standalone probe"},{"id":"p42s1","text":"`scripts/mcp_status.py` runs without the UI:"},{"id":"p43s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p44s1","text":"Exit code `1` means at least one server is dead, `0` means all answered — handy
for cron."},{"id":"p45s1","text":"## Troubleshooting"},{"id":"p46s1","text":"| Symptom | Cause / fix |"},{"id":"p47s1","text":"[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p48s1","text":"## Limitations"},{"id":"p49s1","text":"- The route is a plain `webServer` route, not an authenticated `/api` route. It
exposes only names, "},{"id":"p49s2","text":"endpoints and states on loopback, but if you bind DSH to a
non-loopback address, this route is reach"},{"id":"p49s3","text":"able too.
- The EDT block is 1C-specific; elsewhere it simply finds no projects.
- The client half r"},{"id":"p49s4","text":"eceives no configuration (DSH creates client entries without
it), so all tuning lives in the host ro"},{"id":"p49s5","text":"eives no configuration (DSH creates client entries without
it), so all tuning lives in the host row."}],"truncated":true}
